method.value: Compared repeated 100 GHz images and dropped the first Dec 16 image, which was 3.3% brighter

validation.value: Total flux RMS of 0.2% across four 100 GHz images

evidence.quote: The total flux of the sun was remarkably stable, with an RMS of 0.2%.

method.value: Tb as function of distance from disk center after masking bright and dark features; disk ellipticity taken into account

evidence.quote: we calculated the brightness temperature, $T_b$, as a function of distance from the disk center, $r$

validation.value: Compared with high-resolution images near east limb (100 GHz) and south pole (239 GHz); reliable up to r~960''

evidence.quote: we are safe in using measurements up to $r\simeq960$$''$

method.value: Fit Voigt function to CLV derivative near limb; deconvolve with Voigt, reconvolve with Gaussian core

evidence.quote: we deconvolved with the Voigt function and reconvolved with the Gaussian core

fitting.value: Voigt function fit to derivative of CLV

evidence.quote: this was better fitted with a Voigt function rather than with a Gaussian

method.value: Assumed Te = a1 + a2 ln tau; Tb(mu)=a1+a2(ln mu - gamma); least-squares fit; data reduced to common reference frequency using f^-2 absorption

evidence.quote: The coefficients $a_1$ and $a_2$ can be determined by least square fit of the observations.

key_parameters.value: ALMA data used up to theta~70 deg

evidence.quote: we used ALMA measurements up to $\theta\simeq70$$^\circ$

assumptions.value: LTE thermal free-free and H- absorption proportional to f^-2

evidence.quote: both the free-free and the H$^-$ absorption coefficients are proportional to $f^{-2}$

fitting.value: Least squares on logarithmic form; residual RMS ~60 K

evidence.quote: The fit was very good, with an RMS of residuals of $\sim60$ K

validation.value: Adding a quadratic term did not change results; power series unstable; compared with Eddington-Barbier and models

evidence.quote: the addition of a quadratic term in ([\[logform\]](#logform)) did not change appreciably either the data fit or the inversion results

findings_qualitative.value: ALMA images closely resemble AIA 1600 Å images; plage stands out in the 239/100 GHz ratio while faculae and filament lanes do not

claims.hypothesis: Does the electron temperature vary with optical depth consistent with chromospheric models?
claims.experiment: Inverted CLV curves at 100 and 239 GHz plus Bastian 353 GHz with a logarithmic Te(tau)
claims.result: Linear in ln tau for 0.34<tau100<12, slope -608 K; ~5% below FAL93 model C
claims.finding: Te is consistent with the average quiet-Sun model C and not with the cell-interior models

evidence.quote: Our results are 5% lower than predicted by the average quiet sun model C of Fontenla et al. (1993)

claims.hypothesis: Is limb brightening present at mm wavelengths?
claims.result: Slow but statistically significant increase toward the limb
claims.finding: Slight limb brightening at both frequencies

evidence.quote: with a slow but statistically significant increase towards the limb

why_this_method.value: A parametric logarithmic form is more stable than direct numerical inversion

evidence.quote: which is a more stable procedure than a direct numerical inversion

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Power series expansion of Te(tau) needed at least six terms and gave oscillatory, unphysical inversions

evidence.quote: it gave an oscillatory (hence unphysical) inversion result

limitations_admitted.value: 100 GHz results 30-55'' from the limb may be affected by the 60'' beam

evidence.quote: which may have been affected by the 60$''$ antenna beam
